title: lp_doc v3.0 — the LP-HTML v9 content model (grades 6-12)
description:
THE one content model for a Rumi 6-12 lesson plan, rebuilt to team-docs/lp_format_requirements_6_12.md (the format spec) after the expert's annotated review of a printed G10 Math LP.

WHAT CHANGED FROM 2.0 (all breaking, hence the version bump; template_version goes to v9):
  • CLOSED HEADING SYSTEM. Teaching flow is exactly O -> I -> D -> A -> C -> H, then the
    reference block A..H. `objectives` is now ONE BOX (outcome + the '✓ By the end you can
    answer…' line + 2-3 objectives, each with its own SLO code) — spec §3 O.
  • THE WARM-UP MOVED INSIDE THE INTRODUCTION (spec §2). It is no longer a top-level key and
    no longer its own section: `sections[id=introduction].warmup`. Its items gain the
    `scaffold` kind — 'prior knowledge alone is not a warm-up' (spec §3 I).
  • `say` IS GONE from the block vocabulary. Spec §8: no Ask/Say script, ever. The schema is
    the enforcement; lint's NO_SAY_BOX catches the same shape smuggled into prose.
  • Development must CITE THE TEXTBOOK BY PAGE (`textbook_page`) and may carry a `video`
    (operator override of format-doc §8, 2026-09-01: every LP, all subjects).
  • Conclusion gains `checkpoint` (board-phrased question + mark scheme), `exit_ticket` and
    `reteach_rule` — spec §3 C.
  • Homework is DATA, not prose: `sections[id=homework].homework.items[]`, each tagged
    [SLO code, K/U/A], MCQ-weighted, with its answer ONLY in the reference block (spec §3 H).
  • Every question-bearing item may carry a `ref`; every reference-block answer MUST carry the
    `ref` of the question it answers (the expert's 'model answers do not say which question
    they answer'). lint's REF_ABSENT resolves them.
  • `sequence` — the strip near the masthead saying where this LP sits (spec §5).

The lp_doc JSON is the ARTEFACT OF RECORD; the PDF is a cache. Every string may carry inline
$...$ / $$...$$ KaTeX and \ce{...} mhchem, and EVERY text-bearing field is run through the
maths pipeline at render time — titles, badges, captions, list items, model answers included.
A row-list like [[1,0],[2,3]] is NOT maths: lint's MATH_LEAK fails it.

The reference block keeps the internal key `page2` from 2.0 on purpose — it is what every
`ur_overlay` pointer in the corpus already addresses, and renaming it would silently break
the Urdu toggle of every migrated doc. It PRINTS as 'Reference'.

lesson_id.description: Stable key, e.g. PK_G7_GSCI_CH1_PHOTOSYNTHESIS. Also the cache key for the rendered PDF.

template_version.description: The RENDER contract this doc was authored against. Bumped from v8 with the closed heading system. Optional; the renderer defaults to v9 for a 3.0 doc.

lint_profile.description: 'full' = every pedagogy gate applies (the only value a teacher-facing LP may carry). 'smoke' = a deliberately tiny fixture that proves the renderer; word budgets and completeness are skipped and lint prints a loud banner. Never ship a 'smoke' doc to a teacher.

provenance.description: Every factual claim in the LP must trace to this page range. printed != pdf; the offset differs per book and is recorded in each 01_page_truth/*.json.

book_stem.description: e.g. grade_7_general_science — the page-truth corpus key

medium.description: Language of INSTRUCTION. Textbook quotations stay in the book's own language regardless (LP_DESIGN_RULES §5).

printed_pages.description: What the teacher sees printed on the page, e.g. '11' or '20-21'

pdf_pages.description: Index into the source PDF, e.g. '13'

source_quality_flags.description: Known defects in the source the LP must not propagate.

brand.description: The DEPLOYMENT's brand — whose name the teacher reads on the page. OPTIONAL, and its absence is meaningful: with no brand the page carries NO brand text at all (white-label). Render-law 13.

chapter_title.description: The chapter's NAME, when the book prints one separately from `chapter`.

version.description: ISO date this lp_doc was authored/revised. Printed in the page footer as v<date>. OPTIONAL — the renderer NEVER invents one.

slo.description: NEVER invented. FBISE examines SLOs, not textbooks.

code.description: e.g. B-10-R-10. null when the book prints an outcome with no code — say so rather than inventing one.

success_criterion.description: DEPRECATED in 3.0 — the '✓ By the end you can answer…' line lives in objectives.by_the_end, inside the O box (spec §3 O). Kept so a 2.0 doc migrates without loss.

lp_type.description: Decides the Development/Activity INTERNALS, never the spine.

period_minutes.description: THE MINUTES RULE (spec §4). The minutes of EVERY section — the introduction's warm-up is inside the introduction's own minutes, and homework is never 0 — must sum to this EXACTLY. lint's PACING_SUM enforces it.

board_weight.description: A masthead BADGE, at most 50 code points (gated by lint, not here, so the failure can explain itself) — e.g. 'FBISE SSC-I · ~8 marks'. NOT a sentence describing the paper: an 82-character badge broke the G9 Bio hero header. null for grades 6-8. Gated by lint's BOARD_WEIGHT.

materials.description: Physical things only, listed ONCE in the footer strip, with textbook page numbers. NO video link here — video lives in Development (spec §4).

sequence.description: The sequence strip near the masthead (spec §5): where this LP sits, what comes next, and the next checkpoint.

checkpoint.description: The next assessment this LP is building towards, e.g. 'Ch. 3 assessment (day 12)'.

objectives.description: Section O — ONE BOX (spec §2/§3). Outcome and objectives are never two stacked blocks.

outcome.description: One outcome, phrased as what the PUPIL can do.

by_the_end.description: The '✓ By the end you can answer…' line, naming the question type and its marks.

items.description: Two or three objectives. Never six — split the LP instead (spec §3 O). Each is modelled, practised in class AND assessed today.

slo_code.description: This objective's own SLO code. null ONLY when the book prints none — never invented.

locally_added.description: true = an application objective this LP adds; it must SAY so.

sections.description: The teaching flow, in order. lint (profile=full) requires exactly introduction, development, activity, conclusion, homework — the closed heading system.

title.description: Override for the printed bar label. Defaults to the localized section name.

minutes.description: Printed as the section's minute badge. 0 prints NO badge — and homework may not be 0 (spec §4 / the expert's '0 min' complaint).

warmup.description: INTRODUCTION ONLY. The warm-up is one row inside the Introduction, never its own section (spec §2). The scaffold for TODAY'S concept comes first.

kind.description: `scaffold` = the step that sets up TODAY'S concept, and it comes first. Prior knowledge alone is not a warm-up (spec §3 I).

from.description: For kind=spaced: which earlier chapter/page it retrieves.

ref.description: Short label a reference-block answer can point at, e.g. 'W1'.

textbook_page.description: DEVELOPMENT ONLY, and REQUIRED there (spec §3 D / reviewer sign-off 7): the printed page of the exercise, worked example, diagram or passage this section teaches from.

video.description: DEVELOPMENT ONLY. Sits next to the content it supports, never in materials. Operator override of format-doc §8 (2026-09-01): every LP, all subjects, best available link, validated live.

why.description: One line: what the teacher plays it FOR.

checkpoint.description: CONCLUSION ONLY (spec §3 C): one board-phrased question with its mark scheme.

exit_ticket.description: CONCLUSION ONLY: one or two items the class answers on the way out.

reteach_rule.description: CONCLUSION ONLY: the threshold and what to redo before the next LP, e.g. 'If more than a third miss item 2, re-do the I-do with a 2x2 before Ch.3 day 4.'

homework.description: HOMEWORK ONLY. Real FBISE past/model-paper items, or textbook questions CITED by page and number. Tests only what was taught today; never repeats a class item; NO answers here — they live in page2.homework_key (spec §3 H).

text.description: The question, FULLY WORDED. Never terse notation, and never carrying its own answer.

slo_code.description: The SLO this item tests. Part of the printed [SLO, K/U/A] tag.

format.description: MCQ-weighted at the board's ratio: at least half the items are 'mcq' (spec §6).

ref.description: Short label the reference block's homework_key points at, e.g. 'H1'.

source.description: Where the item comes from. A textbook item may be CITED rather than rewritten (spec §3 H).

paper.description: e.g. 'FBISE SSC-I 2024, Q3(b)' — VERIFIED citations only.

page2.description: THE REFERENCE BLOCK — A board · B model answers · C mistakes · D differentiation · E exam bank · F homework in full · G next period · H coaching corner. Sits BELOW the teaching flow, clearly marked, explicitly not read aloud. Key kept as `page2` so every existing ur_overlay pointer still resolves.

board_final.description: A — the board at the END of the lesson.

model_answers.description: B — every practice item answered in full, EACH NAMING THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS. An answer whose question is not stated anywhere in the LP is the expert's 'referenced but absent' defect; lint's REF_ABSENT fails it.

ref.description: The `ref` of the question this answers (a warm-up / practice / exit-ticket item, or the conclusion checkpoint).

label.description: Optional human label. The renderer prints the QUESTION itself beside the answer, resolved from `ref`.

mistakes.description: C — what pupils actually write, and the exact question you ask back.

differentiation.description: D — one concrete instruction each. Never narrative.

exam_bank.description: E — the exam surface. Distractor codes are DATA: they exist on every wrong option and are printed ONLY as a teacher note, never beside the option a pupil reads (lint's DISTRACTOR_VISIBLE).

answer.description: The correct option, as its letter (A/B/C/D) or its full text.

distractor_codes.description: One short misconception code per WRONG option, in option order.

how_marked.description: One line naming what scores nothing and what scores half (spec §6).

homework_key.description: F — the homework worked through in FULL, textbook questions included. This is the ONLY place a homework answer may appear.

ref.description: The `ref` of the homework item this solves.

item.description: Optional echo of the question. The renderer resolves the real wording from `ref`.

next_period.description: G — names the next LP and what it builds on, with the SLO code where there is one (spec §3 G).

not_going.description: G — what NOT to teach yet, and why.

coaching_lookfor.description: H — DIRECT INSTRUCTION to the teacher about the observable move, drawn from THIS lesson. Never a question put to her (spec §8; lint's NO_SAY_BOX): the question half of the corner is `coaching_reflection`.

coaching_reflection.description: H — ONE question the teacher asks HERSELF after THIS lesson, about HER OWN practice: her class, her pupils, or what she re-teaches next. Ends in a question mark. Never a question about the subject's content (that is the pupils' question, not hers) and never generic. Ported from the K-5 coaching-corner pattern (`wrap.reflection`); gated by lint's COACHING_CORNER. The record-and-send offer that sits beside it is renderer furniture, not authored here.

one_screen.description: The ~200-word WhatsApp message body. The PDF is the attachment.

ur_overlay.description: THE URDU TOGGLE. Keys are RFC-6901 JSON Pointers into THIS document; values replace the English string under `--lang ur`. Frozen: /slo/text_verbatim, anything under /page2/exam_bank, and any `board` block's text.

diagram_spec.description: Handed verbatim to diagrams/index.js -> renderDiagram(spec) -> SVG string.

block.description: One renderable unit. Exactly one vocabulary — the renderer switches on `type` and nothing else. NOTE: `say` was REMOVED in 3.0. Spec §8 bans scripted talk outright.

closes_hook.description: true = this paragraph's FIRST SENTENCE closes the lesson's hook (spec §3 D). Development's first block must carry it.

oneOf.description: A question the teacher asks, with what a good answer contains.

look_for.description: The `Look for:` line — what a right answer sounds like (spec §3 I).

hook.description: true = the lesson's provocation. Exactly one per LP, in the introduction.

closed_by.description: The `id` of the block that ANSWERS this hook. In v9 it must be development's FIRST block.

oneOf.description: ⚠ WATCH OUT — the predictable wrong turn.
ON THE BOARD — what must be left visible.
Vocabulary pre-teach. Belongs in the Introduction, WITH its textbook page (spec §3 I).

page.description: The printed page the words are pre-taught from. Required in the introduction by lint.

title.description: Overrides the printed "Key points" label. Pass "" to print no label.

oneOf.description: I DO — fully worked, numbered, in front of the class.

prompt.description: The question, FULLY WORDED. A page citation alone is not a question (lint's UNWORDED_Q).

oneOf.description: WE DO — guided, 1-2 steps blanked. Comes BEFORE the independent practice, and is timed (spec §3 A).
YOU DO — graded items with answers alongside, SUPPORT/EXTENSION tagged.

minutes.description: Both the guided and the independent beat carry their own minutes (spec §3 A).

cite.description: Textbook exercise this is taken from, e.g. 'Ex 3.2 Q1-Q4, p.68'. Solved in full in the reference block.

ref.description: Short label a model answer points at, e.g. 'P3'.

oneOf.description: The two side-by-side cards: a simplified starter and an early-finisher stretch.
Two blocks side by side as CARDS. Never side-by-side BODY TEXT (D4).
A REAL figure from the book, used as 'as in your book, p.N' reference art.
Display maths. Body text carries inline $...$ instead. A MATRIX always renders display-style — never a subscript hack, never a row-list.
Display chemistry (mhchem). `tex` is the INSIDE of \ce{...}.
